findings.reason: parse_link_destination.mjs:52 now hits `break` at a backslash that comes before a space, so result.pos lands on the backslash. In link.mjs:55-58 the whitespace skip stops at that backslash, the title parse fails, and the `)` check at line 76 sees `\`. The link is rejected, where before it was accepted with the backslash kept as a literal character. For `[a](\ )`, the `start === pos` check at line 70 now returns not-ok immediately.
findings.claim: When an unbracketed link destination contains a backslash followed by a space, it now ends before the backslash. As a result, valid links and reference definitions such as `[x](foo\ "t")` and `[x]: foo\ ` are rejected.
findings.evidence: The diff swaps `if (str.charCodeAt(pos + 1) === 0x20) { pos++; continue }` for `{ break }`. In CommonMark a backslash before a space is a literal character, not an escape. The old code kept the backslash in the destination and then stopped at the space (line 46). The new code ends the destination at the backslash, so `result.pos` points at `\`. In lib/rules_inline/link.mjs:55-58 the whitespace skip stops at `\`; parseLinkTitle then fails, and the following `)` check finds `\`, so the link is rejected. The same happens in image.mjs and reference.mjs, which expect whitespace or end of line after the destination. For `[a](\ )`, `start === pos` (line 70) now returns not-ok outright.
